title: Finite-cover exact sequence for a local system on the complement of a divisor
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and algebraically closed field $k$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], and use sheaves of $A$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $X$ be a normal separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $i:Z=V(f)\hookrightarrow X$ be an effective principal Cartier divisor, meaning that $f$ is a non-zero-divisor in every local ring [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $U=X\setminus Z$ and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For a generic point $\xi$ of a component of $Z$, every constructible etale sheaf $F$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] on $X$ with $i^*F=0$ becomes $j_!G$ for a finite locally constant sheaf $G$ on $U$ after replacing $X$ by an open neighbourhood of $\xi$ (and restricting $Z,U,i,j,F$).

For any finite locally constant $G$ on $U$, there is a finite etale surjection $p:U'\to U$ trivializing $G$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $q:X'\to X$ be the normalization extending $p$: on each component of $X$ it is the disjoint union of the relative spectra of the integral closures of $\mathcal O_X$ in the function fields of the components of $U'$. Then $q$ is finite, $X'$ is normal, $Z'=q^{-1}Z$ is an effective principal Cartier divisor, and $U'=X'\setminus Z'$. With $j':U'\hookrightarrow X'$ and $G'=\operatorname{coker}(G\to p_*p^*G)$, the sheaf $G'$ is finite locally constant and there is a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow j_!G\longrightarrow q_*j'_!p^*G\longrightarrow j_!G'\longrightarrow0.$$
Moreover $Rq_*j'_!p^*G=q_*j'_!p^*G$ and $q^*j_!G=j'_!p^*G$. Geometric stalks of $q_*$ are finite products of the stalks over the given geometric point; $q_*$ is exact on etale $A$-module sheaves. Each point of $Z'$ over a generic point of a component of $Z$ is generic in a component of $Z'$.
